SUBJECT: RESOLUTION NO SA 26-03 – AUTHORIZING THE ISSUANCE AND SALE OF
  TAX ALLOCATION REFUNDING BONDS IN THE PRINCIPAL AMOUNT OF
  NOT TO EXCEED $35,000,000; AND APPROVING A FORM OF INDENTURE
  OF TRUST, A FORM OF ESCROW AGREEMENT, AND A FORM OF BOND
  PURCHASE AGREEMENT, AND AUTHORIZING CERTAIN ACTIONS IN
  CONNECTION THEREWITH

Background:

Pursuant to Assembly Bill No. 1X 26, as modified by Assembly Bill No. 1484 and as further
modified by Senate Bill No. 107, which added Parts 1.8 and 1.85 to Division 24 of the Health
and Safety Code (the “Dissolution Act”), the former Norwalk Redevelopment Agency (the
“Former Agency”) was dissolved on February 1, 2012 and the Successor Agency to the
Norwalk Redevelopment Agency (the “Successor Agency”) was vested with all authority,
rights, powers, duties and obligations of the Former Agency.

Section 34177.5(a)(1) of the Health and Safety Code authorizes successor agencies to
refinance outstanding debt obligations to produce debt service savings. A successor agency
is generally not permitted to issue bonds that would increase the overall indebtedness of the
successor agency or provide additional proceeds to be expended, but it can issue bonds to
refund prior debt obligations and effectuate debt service savings. In such circumstances, the
successor agency’s debt service payments will be reduced, and a former redevelopment
agency’s affected taxing entities will receive additional revenues as residual Redevelopment
Property Tax Trust Fund distributions. Successor Agency staff has identified such an
opportunity which is presented in this report.

On November 8, 2005, the Former Agency issued two series of tax allocation bonds: 1) Tax
Allocation Refunding Bonds, 2005 Series A (Merged Project Area), and 2) Tax Allocation
 Successor Agency to the Norwalk Redevelopment Agency  March 17, 2026

Bonds, 2005 Series B (Merged Project Area) (Taxable) (the “Outstanding TABs”), in the original
principal amount of $64,125,000, of which $32,220,000 is currently outstanding.

Due to favorable market conditions, there is an opportunity to refinance the Outstanding TABs
for debt services savings. Staff recommends that the Board of Directors of the Successor
Agency (the “Board”) adopt the attached Resolution approving the issuance of tax allocation
refunding bonds in one or more series (“2026 Bonds”) in an aggregate principal amount not to
exceed $35,000,000, or such lesser amount as is sufficient to refund all or a portion of the
Outstanding TABs. The refunding of the Outstanding TABs is estimated to result in debt service
savings of approximately $71,863 over the remaining life of the Outstanding TABs. In addition,
the final maturity of the Outstanding TABs will be shortened by one (1) year via the 2026 Bonds.
The reduction in annual debt service payments and remaining repayment term is estimated to
increase tax revenues available for distribution to the Former Agency’s affected taxing entities
as residual tax revenues from the Successor Agency’s Redevelopment Property Tax Trust
Fund. The net proceeds of the 2026 Bonds would be used to refund the Outstanding TABs and
pay costs of issuance.

The trustee of the Outstanding TABs holds certain unexpended proceeds of the Outstanding
TABs in the debt service reserve accounts or subaccounts established for the Outstanding
TABs (collectively, the “Unspent Proceeds”). In connection with the refunding of the
Outstanding TABs, the Successor Agency proposes to transfer all Unspent Proceeds to the
City of Norwalk (the “City”) for expenditure in accordance with the original bond covenants as
permitted under Section 34191.4(c)(1) of the Health and Safety Code. The Unspent Proceeds
currently total approximately $5.3 million on deposit in the debt service reserve accounts or
subaccounts established for the Outstanding TABs. Of said amount, approximately $4.3 million
from the reserve accounts or subaccounts are estimated to be available to be transferred to
the City for expenditure in accordance with the original bond covenants. The estimated
remainder of approximately $973,000 from the original debt service reserve accounts are
anticipated to be used to defease Outstanding TABs as permitted under Section 34191.4(c)(1)
of the Health and Safety Code.

Any Unspent Proceeds that are transferred to the City will be used for redevelopment
purposes, subject to compliance with federal tax rules, as applicable. All unspent proceeds
transferred to the City will be subject to the terms of the Housing Bond Proceeds Funding
Agreement or the Non-Housing Bond Proceeds Funding Agreement, as applicable, previously
entered by the Successor Agency and the City. The City, on behalf of the Successor Agency,
has identified the redevelopment projects below as eligible for funding with Unspent Proceeds
(approximately $4.3 million), together with $17.9 million of other unspent bond proceeds
previously transferred to the City per Department of Finance approval. This list is preliminary
and may be updated as additional information becomes available. In the event any portion of
the Unspent Proceeds cannot be spent in a manner consistent with the original bond
covenants, staff will cause such portion to be used to defease the Outstanding TABs as
permitted under Section 34191.4(c)(1) of the Health and Safety Code.

If the Board approves the issuance of the 2026 Bonds, the Los Angeles County Fourth
Supervisorial District Consolidated Oversight Board (the “County Oversight Board”) will
consider approving the refunding and use of Unspent Proceeds at its meeting on April 21,
2026. Additionally, staff will return to the Board for approval of the Preliminary Official
Statement and Continuing Disclosure Certificate related to the 2026 Bonds. If the Oversight
Board approves the issuance of the 2026 Bonds, then the Oversight Board action will be
subject to approval by the Department of Finance (“DOF”). Pursuant to Section 34177.5(f) of
the Health and Safety Code, DOF has up to 65 days to review the Oversight Board’s action,
which process is expected to conclude in late June 2026.

As shown in the Municipal Advisor Report attached hereto as Attachment 5, based on market
conditions as of February 20, 2026, it is anticipated that a current refunding of the Outstanding
TABs will produce net present value savings of approximately $85,304 over the life of the 2026
Bonds. However, the total level of savings will depend upon market conditions at the time the
2026 Bonds are priced.

The reduction in annual debt service payments frees up additional property tax revenues for

The Resolution also approves forms of the following documents together with any changes or
additions deemed advisable and approved by any Authorized Officer:

Indenture of Trust between the Successor Agency and The Bank of New York Mellon Trust
Company, N.A. (the “Trustee”), which sets forth the terms and provisions relating to the 2026
Bonds and whereby the Trustee agrees to certain rights and duties related to the 2026 Bonds.

Form of Escrow Agreement between the Successor Agency and the Escrow Agent (The Bank
of New York Mellon Trust Company, N.A.), containing terms by which the Escrow Agent will
hold the 2026 Bond proceeds on behalf of the owners of the Outstanding TABs to pay and
discharge these bonds on the redemption date, and give proper notice to the owners.

Bond Purchase Agreement between the Successor Agency and the Underwriter of the 2026
Bonds (Cabrera Capital Markets LLC), pursuant to terms and provisions of which the 2026
Bonds will be sold with a negotiated method of sale, such terms and provisions including an
underwriter’s discount not to exceed 0.75% of the principal amount of the 2026 Bonds.

It is anticipated that staff will return to the Successor Agency for approval of the Preliminary
Official Statement and Continuing Disclosure Certificate related to the 2026 Bonds in April 2026.
The Preliminary Official Statement and Continuing Disclosure Certificate will be required to
market and sell the 2026 Bonds.

In accordance with California Government Code Section 5852.1, good faith estimates of certain
financial aspects of the 2026 Bonds are provided with respect to the 2026 Bonds as an
attachment to the Resolution.

Fiscal Impact:

An estimated $71,863 in total debt service savings would be generated by refinancing the
Outstanding TABs which will be distributed among various taxing entities, including the City. In
addition, it is currently estimated that in connection with the refunding, approximately $4.3
million from the reserve accounts or subaccounts are proposed to be transferred to the City for

  A RESOLUTION OF THE SUCCESSOR AGENCY TO THE NORWALK
  REDEVELOPMENT AGENCY AUTHORIZING THE ISSUANCE AND

  WHEREAS, the Norwalk Redevelopment Agency (the “Former Agency”) was a
public body, corporate and politic, duly created, established and authorized to transact
business and exercise its powers under and pursuant to the provisions of the Community
Redevelopment Law (Part 1 of Division 24 of the Health and Safety Code of the State of
California (commencing with Section 33000) (the “Law”), and the powers of the Former
Agency included the power to issue bonds for any of its corporate purposes; and

  WHEREAS, a redevelopment plan for a redevelopment project known and
designated as the “Merged Project Area” (the “Project Area”) within the City of Norwalk,
California (the “City”) was adopted and approved (as amended and restated, the
“Redevelopment Plan”), in compliance with all requirements of the Law, and all
requirements of law for and precedent to the adoption and approval of the Redevelopment
Plan, have been duly complied with; and

  WHEREAS, on June 28, 2011, the California Legislature adopted ABx1 26 (the
“Dissolution Act”) and ABx1 27 (the “Opt-in Bill”); and

  WHEREAS, the California Supreme Court subsequently upheld the provisions of
the Dissolution Act and invalidated the Opt-in Bill, resulting in the dissolution of the
redevelopment component of the Former Agency as of February 1, 2012; and

  WHEREAS, the Former Agency’s redevelopment powers, assets and obligations
were transferred on February 1, 2012 to the Successor Agency to the Norwalk
Redevelopment Agency (the “Successor Agency”); and

  WHEREAS, on or about June 27, 2012, the Dissolution Act was amended
pursuant to AB1484, adopted as a trailer bill in connection with the 2012-13 California
Budget; and

  WHEREAS, prior to its dissolution, the Former Agency issued its Norwalk
Redevelopment Agency, Tax Allocation Bonds, 2005 Series A (Merged Project Area),
and its Norwalk Redevelopment Agency, Tax Allocation Bonds, 2005 Series B (Taxable)
(Merged Project Area) (collectively, the “Prior Bonds”); and

  WHEREAS, Section 34177.5(a)(1) of the Health and Safety Code authorizes
successor agencies to refund outstanding bonds or other indebtedness provided that
(i) the total interest cost to maturity on the refunding bonds or other indebtedness, plus
the principal amount of the refunding bonds or other indebtedness, does not exceed the
 total remaining interest cost to maturity on the bonds or other indebtedness to be
refunded, plus the remaining principal of the bonds or other indebtedness to be refunded,
and (ii) the principal amount of the refunding bonds or other indebtedness does not
exceed the amount required to defease the bonds or other indebtedness to be refunded,
to establish customary debt service reserves and to pay related costs of issuance
(collectively, the “Savings Parameters”); and

  WHEREAS, the Successor Agency now desires to authorize and approve the
issuance of one or more series of tax allocation refunding bonds (collectively, the “2026
Bonds”) in an aggregate principal amount sufficient to refund all or a portion of the Prior
Bonds, and to irrevocably set aside proceeds of the 2026 Bonds in one or more separate
escrow funds or accounts which will be used to refund the outstanding Prior Bonds being
refunded, to pay costs in connection with the issuance of the 2026 Bonds and to make
certain other deposits as required by the Indenture (as defined below); and

  WHEREAS, the Successor Agency has caused its municipal advisor, Kosmont
Financial Services (the “Municipal Advisor”), to prepare an analysis (the “Municipal
Advisor Work Product”) to demonstrate that the issuance of the 2026 Bonds to refund the
Prior Bonds will meet the Savings Parameters; and

  WHEREAS, the 2026 Bonds will be secured by a pledge of property tax revenues
authorized by Section 34177.5(a) and (g) of the Health and Safety Code, and will be
issued pursuant to the provisions of Article 11 of Chapter 3 of Part 1 of Division 2 of Title 5
of the California Government Code; and

  WHEREAS, under Section 34191.4(c)(1) of the Health and Safety Code, a
successor agency may expend bond proceeds derived from bonds issued on or before
December 31, 2010, in excess of amounts needed to satisfy approved enforceable
obligations, in a manner consistent with the original bond covenants, and if such proceeds
cannot be spent in said manner, the proceeds shall be used to defease the bonds or to
purchase those same outstanding bonds on the open market for cancellation; and

  WHEREAS, pursuant to Sections 34178(a) and 34180(h) of the Health and Safety
Code, with the approval of its oversight board, the Successor Agency may enter into
agreements with the City; and

  WHEREAS, pursuant to Resolution No. OB 14-09 and Resolution No. OB 14-12,
adopted by the former Oversight Board of the Successor Agency to the Norwalk
Redevelopment Agency (the “Former Oversight Board”) on September 22, 2014, the
Former Oversight Board approved, and the Successor Agency entered into, a Housing
Bond Proceeds Funding Agreement and a Non-Housing Bond Proceeds Funding
Agreement (collectively, the “Bond Proceeds Funding Agreements”) with the City; and

  WHEREAS, pursuant to the Bond Proceeds Funding Agreements, certain
proceeds derived from the Prior Bonds for housing and non-housing related
redevelopment projects in excess of amounts needed to satisfy approved enforceable
obligations were previously transferred to the City for use in a manner consistent with the

  WHEREAS, the Board now wishes to approve the issuance and sale of the 2026

DETERMINES, RESOLVES, AND ORDERS AS FOLLOWS:

  SECTION 1. All of the recitals herein contained are true and correct and the Board
so finds.

  SECTION 2. The Board hereby finds that there are significant potential savings
available to the Successor Agency and to applicable taxing entities in compliance with
the Savings Parameters as a result of the use of proceeds of the 2026 Bonds to refund
the Prior Bonds as described herein, as evidenced by the Municipal Advisor Work
Product, which Municipal Advisor Work Product is hereby approved.

basis, and from time to time, in an aggregate principal amount of not to exceed
$35,000,000, or such lesser amount as is sufficient to refund all or a portion of the Prior
Bonds for the purpose of achieving debt service savings in accordance with the Savings
